newsitem.title: FRANCE: French TAT airline union calls 24-hour strike.
newsitem.headline: French TAT airline union calls 24-hour strike.

text.p: The trade union representing airline attendants has called a one-day strike on Tuesday over staffing and work conditions at the French carrier TAT, which is owned by British Airways.
The strike has been called for 24-hours from midnight on Monday (2300 GMT) and will be the third since the start of October.

"Hostesses and stewards at the French unit owned 100 percent by British Airways want to protest against chronic understaffing and the weakening of job contracts," the SNPNC union said in a statement issued hours before the strike was due to begin.
The statement gave no further details.

British Airways hopes to eat further into the French airline market with a recent 780-million-franc offer via TAT and French bank Banque Rivaud to take over troubled French domestic carrier Air Liberte.
